Meeble: Beastmen tribe encountered as enemies during Meeble Burrows expeditions (Ghoyu's Reverie, Ruhotz Silvermines, Everbloom Hollow); certain members (e.g. Meeble Augur, Meeble Scribe) are non-hostile NPCs. Monk-type, Earth Crystal.
All are MNK-type and can Guard and Counter physical attacks; while passive they may sit down and fall asleep, and asleep Meebles will not aggro or link.
Detect by Sound (and True Sound). Weak to Fire, Ice, Earth, Lightning and Light (+15%); resist Water (-40%); no physical resistances.

Base kit: Drill Claw (conal, Max HP Down -75% + Knockback), Thrashing Assault (5-hit + Defense Down), Meeble Warble (AoE call that links awake Meebles, Damage + Silence). Puncturing Frenzy (conal physical) is Notorious Monster only.
Moogle: Beastmen descended from the fallen Kingdom of Kupalika. The great majority of the Moogle bestiary category are non-hostile service NPCs (Nomad, Porter, Curio Vendor, Greeter, Dealer, etc.) and are not tracked here as combat mobs.
No published Crystal, detection, or resistance data for the family. Typical jobs across members: Warrior, Monk, Thief, White Mage, Red Mage and Black Mage.
The combat-relevant member tracked here is Bozzetto Voyager Moogle (Ambuscade).
Orcish Warmachine: Beastmen war machines built and operated by the Orcs (Related: Orc). Warrior-type, Fire Crystal. Detect by Sight (plus Scent; some have True Sight); the "Night Vision" trait widens aggro range at night.
Weak to Fire (+59%, flammable) and to Ice, Wind, Lightning, Water and Light (+30%); resist Earth (-50%) and Dark (-50%).

Base kit: Blastbomb (frontal fire + Bind), Burst (single physical), Fire Arrow (single fire), Firebomb (AoE fire), Fountain (frontal water). NM-only moves: Scatter Shell (~1000 physical split among targets, long cast), Sticky Grenade (AoE physical + Weight), Tear Grenade (AoE physical + Silence + Blind).

Despoil yields Meat Jerky / Dhalmel Steak / Buffalo Jerky (Attack Down). Cogtooth Skagnogg steps through its kit by HP% and only uses the three grenade/shell moves below 20%; Kegpaunch Doshgnosh is immune to Bind, Gravity and Sleep.
Orc: Orcs are the Beastmen of the San d'Oria (Ronfaure) region; related to the Orcish Warmachine siege engines they build.
Base (Green Orc & Overlord) resistances: neutral to Fire and Ice; weak to Water (+50%) and to Wind/Lightning/Light/Earth/Dark (+30%); no physical resistance.
Dark Orcs (Dynamis) shift the grid: resist Fire and Ice (-15%), weak to Water (+30%) and the other elements (+15%).

Armored Orcs (Wings of the Goddess [S] areas) are heavily elemental-resistant: Fire/Ice -50%, Wind/Lightning/Light/Earth/Dark -30%, Water neutral. A leather-mask Campaign variant shares these Armored values.

Beyond the base kit, Orcs gain restricted moves by context: Orcish Counterstance (WotG areas only); and, for Notorious Monsters only, Berserker Dance, Fanatic Dance, Shoulder Charge, and Tornado Edge (WotG/Dynamis).
Despoil: Meat Jerky, Dhalmel Steak, and Buffalo Jerky (Attack Down).
Poroggo: Poroggo are frog Beastmen: enlarged, bipedal toads created by the frog princess Samariri's magic, who later joined the Mamool Ja Savages. Related to the Frog family.
Typical job Black Mage (sub Bard); Water Crystal.
Detect by True Sound (true-hearing - they aggro through Sneak) and pursue by Scent. Sneak/Invisible do not hide you; the Mamool Ja costume from the Viscous Liquid ??? avoids their hearing.
Very high magic defense. Base (Green) grid: strong to Water -80%, Light -70%, Ice -30%, Earth -15%; weak only to Lightning +15%; neutral to Fire/Wind/Dark. No physical resistance.

Ariri Samariri (red) and Brekekekex (blue) variants share an identical, much heavier all-element grid: Water -95%, Light -80%, Ice -50%, Earth -40%, Fire/Wind/Dark -30%, Lightning -15%, plus a minor (~25%) resistance to one physical damage type.

Base kit: Frog Cheer (self Magic Attack Bonus), Frog Song (single-target Charm), Magic Hammer (damage + MP Drain), Providence (self Haste, then casts Breakga/Graviga/Slowga/Bindga/Death), and Water Bomb (AoE Water damage + Silence). As Black Mages they also cast Waterga I-V, Slow, Addle, and the usual -ga nukes.
Gated moves: Frog Chorus (AoE Charm - Notorious Monsters only) and Quenching Hammer (AoE damage + full Dispel + Aspir, scaling with the target's buff count - Ambuscade only).
Qiqirn: Qiqirn are ratlike Beastmen of the Near East (Treasures of Aht Urhgan): scavengers, merchants, diggers, and treasure-hunters spread across the Alzadaal ruins, Aydeewa, Caedarva Mire, and the Arrapago/Halvung frontier.
Typical jobs Thief and Black Mage; many field adversaries are Ranger. Earth Crystal.
Detect by Sight and Sound (some NMs use the True variants - e.g. Cheese Hoarder Gigiroon detects by Sound). Qiqirn are not a Scent family.
Resistances: strong only to Earth -30%; weak to Wind +30% and to Fire/Light/Ice/Water +15%; neutral to Lightning and Dark. No physical resistance.
Base kit: Cutpurse (removes one equipment piece), Deadeye (conal Defense Down + Magic Def Down), Faze (sight-based Terror), Kibosh (Amnesia), and Sandspray (conal Blindness + Accuracy Down -100).
Strap Cutter (removes/disables 3-5 equipment slots at once) is used by Notorious Monsters only.
Siege Turret: Siege Turrets are stationary siege engines built by the three Beastmen nations; they appear in Campaign as Orcish, Quadav, and Yagudo Turrets.
In Campaign they have +50 Magic Defense (150 total).
The wiki lists no detection, no crystal, no job, and an empty TP-move set - they are passive emplacements. Each turret has its own resist profile.

All three take -50% Magical damage. Orcish Turret: strong to Fire/Ice -50%, Wind/Lightning/Light/Earth/Dark -30%, Water neutral. Quadav Turret: Fire/Water -50%, Lightning -15%, Wind/Light/Ice/Earth/Dark -30%. Yagudo Turret: Wind/Ice -50%, Light -15%, Fire/Lightning/Earth/Water/Dark -30%.
Sahagin: Sahagin are amphibious fish Beastmen of the Elshimo seas - Sea Serpent Grotto, the jungles, and the Mamool Ja-held waters. Typical jobs Dragoon, Monk, White Mage, and Bard; Water Crystal.
Resistances: strong to Water -50%; weak to Lightning +50%, Ice +30%, Wind +15%, Earth +15%; neutral to Fire, Light, Dark.

Base kit: Bubble Armor (dispelable Shell, ~-20% magic damage taken), Hydroball (AoE Water damage + STR Down, scaling with the target's level), Hydro Shot (ranged physical + Knockback + Enmity reset), and Spinning Fin (AoE damage + Stun). Jumping Thrust (single-target, Jump-like) is used only by Dragoon Sahagin.

Notorious Monsters use their job's SP ability: Bard NMs (Denn/Fyuu/Seww) use Soul Voice, White Mage NMs (Meww/Novv) use Benediction, and Dragoon NMs (Mouu) use Call Wyvern - the summoned Sahagin's Wyvern does not despawn when the NM dies.
Despoil: Quus, Coral Butterfly (Magic Defense Down).
Quadav: Family has -5% Max HP compared to other mobs.
Despoil steals: Herb Crawler Eggs (Evasion Down) or Hard-boiled Egg (Defense Down).

Standard (Brown) Quadav resist nothing and are weak to most magic (Lightning most of all). Dynamis (Grey), Armored [S], and Khroma variants progressively resist Fire and Water and blunt those magic weaknesses; Khroma Quadav strongly resist every element.

Gated abilities: Wrath of Gu'Dha (Dynamis & Campaign NMs), Diamond Shell (Wings of the Goddess / Campaign — nullifies physical damage from behind), Ore Lob (Campaign NMs and most Beadeaux [S] NMs), Skull Smash and Shell Charge (certain NMs).
Tonberry: Resistances are consistent across all Tonberry variants (Green, Yellow, Purple); individual Notorious Monsters may differ.
Despoil steals: Poison Flour (Magic Defense Down), Poison Dust, or Venom Dust.
Everyone's Grudge / Everyone's Rancor scale with the target's "Tonberry Hate" (Tonberries killed); Throat Stab cuts HP to ~5% and wipes enmity.
Troll: Gurfurlur (King Troll) strongly resists every element (Fire/Lightning/Ice/Earth ~75%, Light/Dark ~50%, Wind/Water ~30%) and two physical damage types (~33% and 50% in the physical row — columns not yet identified, so not stamped per-mob).
Overthrow and Rock Smash are used only when the Troll is unarmed; Potent Lunge only when it holds a weapon.

Gated abilities: Zarbzan (Ranger Trolls), Drop Hammer / Hammerblow / Hammer-Go-Round / Seismohammer (Hammer Trolls — a weapon-model variant, not identifiable by name so kept to notes), Healing Stomp (Notorious Monsters), and Arcane Stomp / Haymaker / Head Snatch / Incessant Fists / Pleiades Ray / Sledgehammer (King Trolls only).
Velkk: The Velkk are a Beastman tribe of Ulbuka, found mostly in southeast Marjami Ravine and in Ulbuka field zones.
Two types by garb/equipment: Warrior-type (red garb, Voay Sword — Warrior/Dark Knight) and Mage-type (blue garb, Voay Staff — Black Mage/Red Mage).
Despoil steals Velkk Necklace (Magic Defense Down) or Velkk Mask (Defense Down).
Type-gated abilities: Saurian Slide (Warrior-type), Saurian Swamp (Mage-type), Jungle Wallop (NM Warrior-type only), Jungle Hoodoo (NM Mage-type only).
Yagudo: The Yagudo are the birdlike Beastman tribe of the Windurst region (Castle Oztroja / Giddeus / Sarutabaruta).
Multiple resistance profiles by variant: base Yagudo; Dark Yagudo (Dynamis); Armored Yagudo [S]; Campaign NMs / White Yagudo [S]; and Tzee Xicu the Manifest each have their own grid.
White Yagudo (e.g. Yagudo Genja, Soo Luma the Ascended in the Shadowreign era) have +30 / +33 extra Magic Defense respectively.
Despoil steals Roast Carp / Roast Pipira (Attack Down), Boiled Tuna Head or Sole Sushi (Accuracy Down) — Castle Oztroja [S] only.
Gated abilities (Notorious Monster / Dynamis / Campaign only): Doom, Feathered Furore, Dark Invocation, Shirahadori.
Craver: Empty-type. Each Craver has an elemental "Core" that fixes its resistances — swipe the resist grid to the Core you are facing.
Material Fend grants a substantial Evasion Bonus and must be dispelled.
Impalement (NM only) leaves the target near death (~5% HP) and fully resets its enmity; mitigated by Sentinel's Scherzo, Migawari: Ichi, Earthen Armor, or an Automaton's Schurzen attachment.
View Sync (NM only) draws in all players within ~25 yalms; Carousel follows it as a combo and is never used stand-alone.
Gorger: Empty-type. Each Gorger has an elemental "Core" that fixes its resistances — swipe the resist grid to the Core you are facing. Each Core resists its own element and the one it beats on the wheel, and is weak to the element that beats it.
Possess the Magic Defense Bonus trait and are aspirable. Gorgers in the original three Promyvions likely have +10 MDB; those in Promyvion-Vahzl have +12 MDB.

Blessing Sync (NM only) copies status enhancements from nearby players, including normally non-dispellable buffs (e.g. Dematerialize, Aftermath). Copying many effects grants a strong Damage Taken reduction — up to full immunity; dispel the stolen buffs to remove it. Enfeebling effects on the Gorger also count toward the reduction.
Receptacle: Stationary Memory Receptacle objects in Promyvion; destroying the correct one opens the portal to the next level.
Published family resistances are unconfirmed (the bestiary lists every cell as unknown).
Seether: Family has an innate defense boost of 20%.
Empty 'Core' family: each Seether has an elemental Core that fixes its resistances — swipe the resist grid to see all eight Core alignments.
Standard Seethers appear in Promyvion; Apex Livid Ragers are the high-tier version in the same zones.
Thinker: Empty 'Core' family: each Thinker has an elemental Core that fixes its resistances — swipe the resist grid to see all eight Core alignments.
Uses tiered drain/absorb moves (Binary/Spirit/Trinary) plus status moves; Shadow Spread is used only by notorious monsters.
Glassy Thinker is a Reisenjima mini-boss with its own fixed resistance profile.
Weeper: Empty-type. Each Weeper has an elemental "Core" that fixes its resistances — swipe the resist grid to the Core you are facing. Each Core resists its own element and the one it beats on the wheel, and is weak to the element that beats it.

Innate -10% Defense penalty. Possess the Magic Defense Bonus trait and are aspirable. Weepers in the original three Promyvions likely have +10 MDB; those in Promyvion-Vahzl have +12 MDB; Apex Woeful Lamenters have +14 MDB.
Each Weeper also has Memory of [its element] — a 10' AoE nuke matching its Core element (e.g. a Fire-Core Weeper uses Memory of Fire).
Wanderer: Empty-type. Each Wanderer has an elemental "Core" that fixes its resistances — swipe the resist grid to the Core you are facing. NOTE the Wind Core differs from other Empty families: it is weak to Ice only (not Ice + Water).
Possess MP and the Magic Defense Bonus trait. Family has an innate Evasion Bonus and a -10% Defense penalty (e.g. Apex Idle Drifters have +40 evasion).
Ghrah: Changes forms over time, roughly every 60-75 seconds. Different forms take on aspects of different jobs and change the moves available. All forms cast magic.
Ball Form (Black Mage): passive; uses Hexidiscs.
Spider Form (Warrior): aggressive; uses Sickle Slash.
Bird Form (Thief): aggressive; uses Damnation Dive.
Humanoid Form (Paladin): aggressive; uses Vorpal Blade.
Jobs may not actually change when shifting forms (unconfirmed).
Elemental resistances follow the Ghrah's current Core element — cycle/swipe the resist grid to see each Core.
Zdei: Possesses a Magic Defense Bonus of +20 (120 total). Aspirable.

Swaps between a No-Ring/Bar mode and Ring/Bar (Ring / Pole) modes. First swap to a Ring/Bar mode is ~10-20 seconds after engaging; stays in No-mode 10-20s and in Ring/Bar modes 50-60s. Will not swap while charging Optic Induration.
Abilities are mode-gated: Normal (no rings/bars) → Optic Induration; Ring mode → Reactor Overheat / Reactor Overload; Pole mode → Decayed Filament / Static Filament. Reactor Cool is used in any mode.
Elemental: Affinity Resistance: an elemental's resistance to offensive elemental magic depends on its element, and it uses spells and abilities based on that element (hybrids use two elements). Cycle/swipe the resist grid to compare each element and hybrid profile.

All five weapon-skill damage types are cut to ~25%; Physical/Magical/Breath still land for full. A pure elemental takes only ~5% from its own element and the element it is strong against, and ~150% from its weakness. Hybrids resist six elements (two at ~5%, four at ~85%) and are weak to two (~150%).
Silence prevents an elemental's TP moves. Some elementals change their resistances during battle.
The Abyssean and Ru'Aun versions of the hybrid elementals (e.g. Ascended, Apex) do not use TP moves.
Heartwing: White Mage-type light elementals: cast Dia, Cure, Regen, Protect, Shell, Banish, and Holy, and carry 20 Magic Defense Bonus.
Strongly resist Light and Dark (~5%) and take ~50% from every other element; Magical and Breath damage are halved. Weak to Piercing and Ranged (200%).
Drift harmlessly around Eastern Ulbuka, trailing after adventurers.
Monoceros: Unicorn elementals: Warrior-type, Fire-aligned. They come in two forms with different resistances — swipe the resist grid between the Monocero (Ixion) and Alicorn profiles. Ixion-named and base members use the Monocero table; Alicorn-named members use the Alicorn table.
Movement Speed +75% while passive, +250% while aggressive.
Monocero form uses Wrath of Zeus and Lightning Spear (thunder); Alicorn form uses Grace of Hera and Scintillant Lance (light). All forms share Acheron Kick, Damsel Memento, and Rampant Stance.
Pixie: Pixies operate on a hate system: at minimum hate they are non-aggressive and will Cure players at yellow or lower HP, and will Raise a defeated player (no EXP loss). There is a long delay between a Pixie's casts.

Defeating Pixies slowly degrades their helpfulness until they eventually become aggressive (the hate regenerates over time), and slowly reduces their population on a server -- raised again by trading Bottled Pixie items to the Fay Spring (Witchfire Glen, a north-western area of Grauberg [S]).

Three resist profiles: base Pixie; Veela and Danaid (stronger elemental resistance, ~60%); Unseelie (the dark court -- strongly resists Dark instead of Light). All three take full physical damage, resist Magical (~25%), and are nearly immune to Wind (~95%).
Casters (White Mage / Black Mage); detect by Magic and Sight; Wind Crystal.
NM-only TP moves: Norn Arrow (~1000 AoE damage + ~1 min Encumbrance) and Eldritch Wind (AoE damage + full Dispel + Addle + Plague).
Porxie: Possesses MP but does not cast.
Single resist profile: near-immune to Wind (-60%), resists all other elements and Light (-50%); weak to Earth (+15%) and to Piercing/Ranged (+12.5%). Slight Magical resistance (-12.5%).
Wind Crystal; detects by Sight and Sound.
Ascended Porxie is the Reisenjima NM; Biune Porxie is a Sortie NM (#B maps).
Umbril: Spawns at night within field zones (may remain up within dungeons). Initially appears within the ground, then climbs out after detecting a player.
Takes double damage from magical breath attacks (e.g. 1,000 Needles) on top of its magic damage reduction.
Despoil: Leafkin Frond (Magic Defense Down) or Umbril Ooze (Attack Down).
Dark Crystal shadow elemental: near-immune to Dark (-95%), weak to Light (+50%) and Fire (+30%); resists most other elements and physical (Slashing/Piercing/Ranged -50%). Detects by Sight and Magic.
Sgili is a Fire-resistant, Earth-weak subspecies (see its notes).
Murex: Passive by day, aggressive at night; the night aggression window widens with the moon phase (as narrow as 23:00-0:00 at the new moon, as wide as 18:00-5:00 at the full moon).
Limule: Passive by day, aggressive at night; the night aggression window widens with the moon phase (as narrow as 23:00-0:00 at the new moon, as wide as 18:00-5:00 at the full moon).
Clionid: Passive by day, aggressive at night; the night aggression window widens with the moon phase (as narrow as 23:00-0:00 at the new moon, as wide as 18:00-5:00 at the full moon).
Amoeban: Passive by day, aggressive at night; the night aggression window widens with the moon phase (as narrow as 23:00-0:00 at the new moon, as wide as 18:00-5:00 at the full moon).
Also uses Vacuole Discharge (no published description). Nucleic Implosion is used only by earth-based Amoeban.
Gyve: Immobile structures. Resistance to elemental offensive magic depends on the element of the Gyve/Fetter.
Has a 20' enfeebling aura; the enfeebling effect is based on the element of the Gyve/Fetter.
Trait — Affinity Resistance: resistance to elemental offensive magic depends on the elemental's element. Includes movement speed and gimmicks (e.g. Silence prevents TP moves).
Structure: Immobile structures, related to the Gyves.
Animated Weapon: Immune to Sleep, Silence, and Stun, but susceptible to Lullaby.
Satellite and Animated Weapons have a Magic Defense of 160.
Members mimic various jobs — each Animated/Satellite weapon type behaves as a specific job.
Avatar: Powerful beings of Vana'diel lore — evoked by Summoners and central to many storylines.

High-Tier Mission Battlefield Prime Avatars (★) have an innate −30% damage reduction to magic, physical, and ranged, plus a potent en-spell of their element. They have four weaknesses — triggered by Weaponskills, Abilities (e.g. Provoke), offensive Magic, and offensive Pet abilities (Ready/Blood Pact/Wyvern breath/Automaton attachments). Triggering one removes the damage penalty or weakens the en-spell; the effect varies per Prime and per trigger.
A proc'd weakness stuns the current action and keeps the Prime weakened until it uses Astral Flow, after which it must be re-proc'd.
Biotechnological Weapon: Legendary machine weapons (伝説の機獣) of ancient Zilart design — the Omega and Ultima model lines and their Prototype, Arch, and Forerunner revisions.

Omega models swap between a four-legged and a two-legged stance, each with its own TP-move set (four-legged resists physical damage, two-legged resists magical); Ultima models are stationary casters that follow Nuclear Waste with an elemental conal attack.
Replica: Dynamis 'Replica' constructs — effigies, idols, tombstones and golems modeled on the Beastmen, found in the Divergence versions of the four original Dynamis zones (and as Prototypes in Dynamis-Tavnazia).

Every Replica uses Seismostomp, plus one signature move set by the Beastman it mimics: Quadav effigies use Lead Breath (Weight), Orc tombstones use Numbing Glare (Paralysis), Yagudo idols use Tormentful Glare (Curse), and Goblin golems use Torpid Glare (Sleep).
Supreme Being: The Supreme Being family collects the 'deity'-class bosses of Vana'diel — beings defined only as gods, greater even than the Avatars (the wiki lists the family as Related to: Avatars).
There is no shared resistance profile or kit — each member (Promathia/Metus, Cloud of Darkness, Hades/Plouton, Provenance Watcher, Shinryu) has its own.
Adversary Avatar: Avatars and elementals summoned by enemy mobs rather than by players.
Blessed Races of Altana: The five races blessed by Altana — Hume, Elvaan, Tarutaru, Mithra and Galka.
Tubes: Crystal War smart bombs designed by Adelheid Sturm to cripple the forces of the Beastmen Confederate. These levitating bombs detonate after a set time once a target is close, and each releases an area-of-effect blast that inflicts a status ailment.

A large number were stolen from Bastok by the Quadav during the raids on Grauberg. The Quadav shared them with the Goblins, who reverse-engineered them into very potent poison-inducing vials and flasks and sold those on to the Orcish Hosts.
Immobile, and despawns after using an ability.
Cannot be charmed and cannot be used in Pankration. Aspir and Drain both work.

Each blast is locked to its own type: Silencing Blast to Silencing Tubes, Binding Blast to Binding Tubes, Paralyzing Blast to Paralyzing Tubes. Noxious Spray carries no such restriction. All four appear in Wings of the Goddess areas.

notes: Published on the category page as "Crimson Robe Variant Resistances": damage-type row identical to the Ordinary set (100 / 75 / 50 / 87.5 / 112.5 / 112.5 / 50 / 50), element row 115 / 100 / 100 / 50 / 30 / 50 / 85 / 30.

PARKED, not applied: the wiki does not say which Corse wear the crimson robe. Giltine is the only member in the screenshot batch whose render is a red-robed figure, but a render is not the sub-type test - a published grid plus known membership is. Ask the user.
